title: This week in recruiting tools: Juicebox buys Fetcher, LinkedIn Hiring Assistant inside iCIMS, Workday ships Candidate Profile and agents
summary: A consolidation week across the recruiting stack: Juicebox agreed to acquire Fetcher's assets, iCIMS wired in LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant, Metaview went deeper into Workday, Workday launched Candidate Profile plus HR agents, Eightfold appointed a new CEO, and Noon published public docs for driving it from AI assistants.

items.headline: Juicebox announced an agreement to acquire Fetcher's assets
items.detail: Announced 6 Oct 2026 (Business Wire; Axios). Fetcher sold batch sourcing on per-role tiers; Juicebox is a natural-language search tool. Fetcher customers should plan for a migration; see Juicebox and Fetcher in the directory and our sourcing-database switching guide.
items.matters: The independent sourcing category keeps shrinking; AI-search vendors are buying customer bases.

items.headline: iCIMS integrated LinkedIn Hiring Assistant into its ATS
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (HRTech Series), two weeks after LinkedIn's 'Hiring Assistant 2' update (TLNT, 2 Oct), which focused on smarter matching.
items.matters: LinkedIn's agent now lives inside a major enterprise ATS, so iCIMS customers get an agent without adding a vendor; the seat and InMail credit model is unchanged. Compare in iCIMS and LinkedIn Recruiter.

items.headline: Metaview expanded its Workday integration for Fortune 500 recruiting teams
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (Business Wire). Metaview records and structures interviews and is extending that into agentic workflows on Workday data (Metaview review).
items.matters: The ATS is becoming the control plane for recruiting agents; point tools without native Workday or SAP integrations will feel it in enterprise deals.

items.headline: Workday launched Candidate Profile and a set of HR, finance and IT agents
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (Workday blog; Investing.com). Candidate Profile is a reusable applicant profile meant to end repeated form-filling.
items.matters: Portable profiles change the apply experience for the largest employers, and Workday's own agent layer now competes directly for third-party automation budget.

items.headline: Eightfold AI named Joe Korngiebel as CEO
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (GlobeNewswire). Eightfold sells talent intelligence, matching and rediscovery to large enterprises.
items.matters: CEO changes at platform vendors usually precede packaging and pricing changes; buyers mid-evaluation should ask about the roadmap and contract flexibility.

items.headline: Noon published public MCP docs, a weekly changelog and switch-from guides
items.detail: Published 14 Oct 2026 (noon.ai/changelog). The docs let Claude and ChatGPT users drive Noon's sourcing and outreach tools from their assistant.
items.matters: First vendor in our directory with public AI-assistant (MCP) documentation; expect 'can my assistant run it?' to become a standard RFP line.

directory: New on RecruitmentTools.org this week: vendor-neutral switching guides for teams leaving LinkedIn Recruiter, SeekOut or hireEZ and Gem.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Workday moves to split up Mobley, HireVue adds fraud signals, Remote builds its own screener
summary: A week where the legal and build questions caught up with the stack: Workday asked the court to decertify the Mobley age collective, HireVue shipped fraud detection across interviews and assessments, Remote's people team showed what an in house ATS looks like, Survale plugged candidate feedback into SmartRecruiters on the SAP Store, Dayforce closed on Ribbon, and the staffing numbers from Bullhorn and Recruit Holdings kept climbing.

items.headline: Workday asked the court to decertify the age discrimination collective in Mobley v. Workday
items.detail: Filed 10 Nov 2026 in federal court in San Francisco, as reported by Startup Fortune citing MLex and Forbes. The collective now covers more than 15,000 opt in plaintiffs. A second filing asks Judge Rita Lin to stop the much wider applicant group from pursuing race, sex, age and disability claims together. Workday argues that employers, not Workday, make the hiring decisions and that each customer configures screening differently. This is a motion, not a ruling.
items.matters: Whatever Judge Lin decides will set how much shared liability a screening vendor carries for its customers' outcomes. Buyers should keep asking vendors for configuration logs and adverse impact reporting now rather than after a ruling.

items.headline: HireVue launched advanced fraud detection inside its platform
items.detail: Announced 10 Nov 2026 via PR Newswire (release text). The new capabilities connect identity, location and behavioral signals across interviews and assessments and present the evidence to hiring teams rather than issuing a verdict on their own.
items.matters: Candidate fraud checks are moving from separate point tools into the interview and assessment layer. Teams already paying for HireVue should test this before buying a standalone identity product.

items.headline: Remote's HR team replaced outside vendors with tools it built using AI, starting with a CV screener
items.detail: Reported 10 Nov 2026 by HR Brew. The project began as a January off site dare between founder Job van der Voort and CPO Barbara Matthews to build an ATS in house; a resume screener came first and grew into a wider rebuild of the internal stack, one homegrown tool at a time.
items.matters: Most companies will not build an ATS, but a credible build option changes renewal conversations. Expect more buyers to ask why a screening add on costs what it does.

items.headline: Survale joined SAP PartnerEdge and listed its SmartRecruiters integration on the SAP Store
items.detail: Announced 10 Nov 2026 (citybuzz). Status changes in SmartRecruiters trigger pulse surveys at each hiring stage, and responses are tied to job, location, source and hiring manager data.
items.matters: SmartRecruiters customers inside the SAP estate get a procurement path for candidate feedback that does not need a separate contract negotiation.

items.headline: Dayforce closed its acquisition of the AI interviewing platform Ribbon
items.detail: Reported 5 Nov 2026 by HR Brew. Ribbon founder Arsham Ghahramani builds conversational AI voice interviews; Dayforce adds them to its HCM suite.
items.matters: Another suite has bought its AI interviewer instead of partnering, which narrows the field of standalone voice screening vendors that integrate everywhere.

items.headline: US staffing hours rose 12% year over year in the week ended 31 October
items.detail: From the SIA | Bullhorn Staffing Indicator published 10 Nov 2026: commercial hours up 13%, professional up 10% and industrial up 18% on the prior year, another year to date high.
items.matters: Agencies heading into peak season on rising hours tend to add recruiters and seats, so renewal leverage sits with vendors through year end.

items.headline: Recruit Holdings reported record quarterly revenue with its HR Technology unit leading
items.detail: Results for the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026, reported 11 Nov by Staffing Industry Analysts: revenue of JPY 1.09 trillion, about USD 6.88 billion, up 19.7%. Recruit is the parent of Indeed.
items.matters: Indeed's owner is growing fast enough to keep pushing sponsored job pricing and its own screening features, which affects every ATS that posts there.

directory: New on RecruitmentTools.org this week: shortlists of nursing staffing agencies, electrical staffing agencies and fashion recruitment agencies, plus city guides for Chicago and Las Vegas.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Ashby builds in an AI interviewer, Joveo and Indeed ship sourcing agents, SAP closes TechWolf
summary: Interviewing and sourcing agents moved into products buyers already own: Ashby put an AI Interviewer in its ATS, Joveo released the contract free Tandem agent, and Indeed opened Smart Screening and Sourcing Assistant to UK subscribers. Fountain let frontline teams build their own agents, Pindrop entered hiring fraud detection, SAP closed TechWolf, Revelio Labs bought SourceStack, and staffing hours kept rising.

items.headline: Ashby shipped an AI Interviewer inside its ATS, with consent and a human review step built in
items.detail: Announced 17 Nov 2026 on Ashby's product updates page. Candidates hold a structured, job specific conversation in the browser, and the hiring team receives a transcript and an evaluation against the role criteria. Candidates see a disclosure and give affirmative consent first, and can ask for an accommodation or a different interview format. All In One customers get 200 interviews included as a one time, non expiring allowance.
items.matters: This is the first time a major mid market ATS has put a first round AI interviewer in the core product rather than a marketplace add on. Ashby customers piloting a separate screening vendor now have a native option to benchmark against, and the free allowance makes a side by side test cheap.

items.headline: Joveo launched Tandem, a prompt driven recruiting agent with no contract required
items.detail: Released 17 Nov 2026 via GlobeNewswire. A recruiter describes the hire in plain language, Tandem drafts the job description for approval, then sources candidates, scores each out of 100 with supporting evidence, and contacts them by email, SMS or both. Applicants chat to apply, complete a recorded AI interview and self book time on the calendar. Joveo says setup takes under five minutes and that the person hiring makes every decision.
items.matters: A programmatic media company selling an end to end agent without a contract is aimed squarely at small teams that never bought enterprise recruitment marketing. Expect other media vendors to copy the self serve packaging.

items.headline: Indeed rolled out Smart Screening and Sourcing Assistant to UK employers at FutureWorks London
items.detail: Reported 18 Nov 2026 by Onrec. Both tools come with Smart Sourcing Professional and Enterprise subscriptions. Sourcing Assistant searches Indeed's pool of 380 million sourceable profiles from natural language instructions, with recruiters approving messages. Indeed's own figures: users save 11.5 hours a week, sourced candidates are 2.9 times more likely to be hired, Smart Screening needs 26% fewer applications per hire, and Interview Automation moves applicants to interviews 42% faster.
items.matters: Indeed is turning its resume database into an agentic sourcing product inside the subscription UK employers already pay for. All four numbers are vendor data, so ask for your own account level baseline before and after switching it on.

items.headline: Fountain introduced Orchestra, a builder for custom AI agents in frontline workforce teams
items.detail: Announced 17 Nov 2026 in Fountain's newsroom. Employers describe hiring and scheduling work in plain language and Orchestra builds agents that use data in Fountain's software and can call workers and applicants. It extends Fountain's hiring and onboarding platform, which the company says serves more than 500 frontline employers.
items.matters: High volume employers have been buying one fixed purpose bot per workflow. A builder lets them automate site specific steps without a new vendor each time, but someone has to own testing and change control for every agent the business creates.

items.headline: Pindrop launched Pindrop for Hiring and earned Microsoft Teams certification for Pulse for Meetings
items.detail: Announced 18 Nov 2026 on Pindrop's news page. AI resume review flags fabricated employment histories, suspicious identities and duplicate applications, and Pulse for Meetings analyzes live interview audio and video for synthetic media, adding voice and location risk signals. Recruiting and security teams use the combined signals to investigate before granting workforce access, and Teams administrators can now surface deepfake warnings inside meetings.
items.matters: A voice security company built for banks and call centers now sells directly to recruiting. With HireVue adding fraud signals last week, teams can choose between checks inside the interview platform and an independent layer that spans every tool.

items.headline: SAP completed its acquisition of TechWolf
items.detail: Closed 16 Nov 2026, per the SAP News Center. SAP plans to make TechWolf's context graph a core of SAP SuccessFactors and a grounding layer for Joule queries about work and skills.
items.matters: Skills inference becomes a native SuccessFactors capability rather than a partner integration. Customers using a separate skills cloud should ask how long SAP will support third party skills data before renewing.

items.headline: Revelio Labs acquired job posting data provider SourceStack
items.detail: Announced 17 Nov 2026 via PR Newswire. SourceStack collects postings directly from employer applicant tracking systems. Terms were not disclosed, and founder Alec Barrett-Wilsdon joined Revelio Labs as General Manager of Sourcing.
items.matters: Postings pulled straight from ATS feeds are cleaner than scraped job board copies, which improves competitor hiring and salary benchmarks. Talent intelligence buyers should expect sharper role level demand data from Revelio in 2027.

items.headline: US staffing hours were up 11% year over year in the latest SIA and Bullhorn indicator
items.detail: Published 17 Nov 2026 by Staffing Industry Analysts. For the week ending 7 Nov, commercial staffing hours rose 13% and professional 9%. Industrial led at 18% and IT grew 4%, while office and clerical fell 8%.
items.matters: Industrial demand is carrying the rebound into peak season while office work keeps shrinking. Staffing firms planning 2027 budgets should weight recruiter headcount and ATS seats toward light industrial desks.

directory: New on RecruitmentTools.org this week: shortlists of aerospace staffing agencies, clinical research staffing agencies and pharmaceutical headhunters, plus city guides for Baltimore and Orlando.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Workday closes C1.ai to govern agent access, BambooHR plugs into ChatGPT, Enhancv flags ghost jobs
summary: A Thanksgiving week where HR systems moved into the chat window and the identity layer: Workday finished buying C1.ai so the worker record also controls what AI agents can reach, and BambooHR shipped a ChatGPT plugin on its MCP server. Salary.com wired Deel data into CompAnalyst, Enhancv started grading job postings for ghost job risk, Hyring moved past hiring, and US staffing hours hit a 2026 high.

items.headline: Workday completed its acquisition of C1.ai and now pitches itself as the identity governance layer for people and AI agents
items.detail: Announced 23 Nov 2026 in the Workday newsroom. C1.ai governs which systems a person or an autonomous agent can access, from business applications to cloud infrastructure, with permissioning, monitoring and real time enforcement. Workday's argument is that every hire, job change and exit is already a Workday event, so access rules should follow that record. In its own post, C1.ai says Workday's record covers more than 11,500 organizations. The deal follows Workday's announced intent on 18 Nov to buy Honeydew, a semantic layer for AI and business intelligence.
items.matters: For recruiting teams the practical change is offboarding and onboarding of agents, not people. As sourcing, screening and scheduling agents multiply inside the HR stack, the question of who approved each agent's access to candidate data will land on whoever owns the Workday tenant. Ask your security team now whether recruiting agents are on that inventory.

items.headline: BambooHR launched a ChatGPT plugin that reads live people data and hiring pipelines within each user's existing permissions
items.detail: Released 24 Nov 2026 via a BambooHR press release. Leaders, managers and employees can run saved reports, check hiring pipelines, update records and request time off from ChatGPT. The plugin runs on the BambooHR MCP, the connection layer the company introduced in October 2026 alongside its Claude connector, and every action is limited to what that person can already see in BambooHR.
items.matters: Small and mid sized companies that use BambooHR's built in hiring module now have two chat front ends for it. That makes permission hygiene inside BambooHR more important, because anything a hiring manager can see becomes something they can ask a chatbot to summarize.

items.headline: Salary.com connected Deel employee data to its CompAnalyst pay platform
items.detail: Announced 23 Nov 2026 via HR News Canada. The integration syncs employee, job and organizational data from Deel into CompAnalyst Plus or Enterprise, so compensation teams can benchmark pay, check internal equity and model the cost of changes without manual uploads. Deel says its data covers 150 countries.
items.matters: Recruiters hiring across borders often quote ranges from stale spreadsheets. When offer ranges come from the same synced data that compensation uses, fewer offers get reworked after the candidate has already seen a number.

items.headline: Enhancv launched a job search that flags likely ghost jobs before candidates apply
items.detail: Released 24 Nov 2026 via EIN Presswire. The resume builder's job search page says it checks 7.5 million postings every hour and rates ghost job risk from signals including posting age, whether a salary is listed, company reviews and how specific the duties and requirements are. Flagged postings stay in results with the reasons shown.
items.matters: Employers do not control this score, but their postings are now being graded in public. Evergreen requisitions with no pay range and vague duties are exactly what gets flagged, so it is worth closing old reqs and posting ranges even where the law does not require it.

items.headline: Hyring, an AI interviewing vendor, added Hyring Insight, a time tracking and workforce intelligence product
items.detail: Announced 23 Nov 2026 in a TechnologyWire release carried on TechCrunch. The Chennai company, which has built AI interviewing and screening software for nearly four years, says Insight records work openly through a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux and uses AI to explain a workday to managers.
items.matters: Another hiring tool is stretching past the offer. Buyers comparing AI interview vendors should ask which product the roadmap actually funds, and anyone in a jurisdiction with employee monitoring rules should check them before bundling the two.

items.headline: US staffing hours reached their 2026 high in the latest SIA and Bullhorn indicator, up 12% year over year
items.detail: Reported 24 Nov 2026 by Staffing Industry Analysts. In the week ended 14 Nov, hours rose 0.3% from the prior week. Commercial staffing was up 14% year over year and industrial up 19%, helped by manufacturing, logistics and data center construction. IT hours slipped 1.9% week over week while staying 4% above last year.
items.matters: Industrial desks remain the growth engine heading into December. Agencies planning 2027 software renewals should size seats and texting volume for that mix rather than for professional placements.
